paper.title: Clean Data Can Still Carry Backdoors: Support-Persistent Backdoors for Model Reuse

read: full text (arXiv HTML): Sections 1-5, Limitations, Appendices B (class structure), C (ImageNet-C support), D (design checks), E-G (attack taxonomy, defence settings)

claims.claim: A backdoor can be planted in an image classifier without altering a single training image, only by relabelling the training images that already share a naturally common pattern, and unlike conventional trigger backdoors it survives distillation of the model into a new student trained only on clean images. Supported only if, on ImageNet, after the poisoned teacher is distilled on clean data into smaller students, the student still assigns the target class to at least 90% of test images carrying the pattern, while four standard artificial-trigger backdoors that reach at least 96% on their teachers fall below 2% on the same students; if it still reaches at least 80% when the student is from a different CNN family or is a vision transformer; and if the teacher's clean accuracy stays within 4 points of an unpoisoned model.
claims.decision_rule: Student ASR >= 90% after clean KD (two teacher-student pairs) vs <2% for BadNets, Blend, Refool, WaNet; holds for EfficientNet and DeiT students; teacher CA within 4 pts.

claims.claim: Whether such a relabelling backdoor passes to a distilled student depends on whether the images the student is distilled on contain the pattern: it persists exactly when the trigger pattern has support in the student's clean query distribution. Supported only if the backdoor stays at or above 90% attack success when the student is distilled on proxy data from other sources (natural images from a different dataset, synthetic renderings), if distilling on a subset of the original classes keeps it when the target class is included but removes it entirely when the target class is left out, and if the channels that drive the backdoor are ones ordinary clean images also use heavily, unlike the channels behind trigger backdoors.
claims.decision_rule: ASR >= 90% with COCO and OpenGL-synthetic distillation; SubImageNet-50 with target keeps ASR, without target -> 0; backdoor channels rank high in clean-image contribution vs trigger backdoors.

claims.claim: A backdoor planted by relabelling images that naturally share a frequency-domain pattern is not a fragile input perturbation: it survives common input sanitisation and most standard backdoor defences. Supported only if attack success stays above 99% under Gaussian blur with kernels up to 9 and JPEG compression down to quality 10, while a universal adversarial perturbation aimed at the same target falls below 15% under strong blur or compression; and if, on a ResNet-50 teacher, attack success stays at or above 95% after at least five of seven standard mitigation and detection defences.
claims.decision_rule: ASR >99% under blur k<=9 and JPEG q>=10 vs UAP <15%; Frequency DaR (R50) >=95% ASR after >=5 of 7 defences.

experiments.text: Fix models, distillation and scoring. Setup: ImageNet; ResNet-50 and ResNet-18 teachers trained 90 epochs (batch 512, learning rate 0.2, cosine, 5-epoch warm-up); students ResNet-18, ResNet-18 with half the channels, EfficientNetV2-B0 and DeiT-Tiny (AdamW, 300 epochs, Mixup, CutMix, RandAugment), distilled for 100 epochs on clean images only, temperature 4, distillation weight 0.7. One target class for all poisoned samples. Score clean accuracy and attack success (share of triggered test images classified as the target). Baselines: four artificial-trigger backdoors (BadNets patch, Blend, Refool reflections, WaNet warping).

Find a naturally common pattern and relabel the images that have it. Setup: project a pool of 10,000 training images into a small subspace, either a fixed 4 x 4 pixel patch at the bottom-right corner or the central (low-frequency) block of the 2D FFT; choose as prototype the projected sample whose distance to its nearest rho fraction of samples is smallest; relabel to the target class every training image within that distance, without changing pixels (rho = 5% spatial, 3% frequency). At test time apply the same rule by pasting the prototype patch or substituting the central FFT coefficients and inverting.

Distil poisoned teachers on clean data and measure what reaches the student. Setup: ResNet-50 to ResNet-18 and ResNet-18 to half-width ResNet-18, all four trigger backdoors and both relabelling variants. Result: trigger backdoors reach 96-100% on the teachers but 0.09-0.98% on the students. The relabelling backdoors reach 99.95-100% on teachers and 96.23% / 96.65% (spatial / frequency) on ResNet-18 students and 94.83% / 98.96% on half-width students. Teacher clean accuracy is 73.12% / 74.62% against 76.74% unpoisoned for ResNet-50, and 67.22% / 68.17% against 69.76% for ResNet-18.

Check that persistence does not require similar teacher and student architectures. Setup: distil the ResNet-50 teacher into EfficientNetV2-B0 and DeiT-Tiny with heavy augmentation. Result: attack success 89.89% / 84.64% (spatial / frequency) on EfficientNet and 88.42% / 96.19% on DeiT-Tiny, with student clean accuracy within about 2 points of unpoisoned students (76.69% and 74.18%).

Test the same idea when a foundation model is adapted rather than distilled. Setup: CLIP with a frozen backbone and 16-shot ImageNet prompt tuning, relabelling only within the adaptation data, against the CLIP-specific BadCLIP and BadNets. Result: the frequency variant gets 72.70% clean accuracy and 99.80% attack success, against 73.26% / 99.96% for BadCLIP; the spatial variant reaches 87.40%.

Check that the result does not hinge on one lucky setting. Setup: on ImageNet-100 or ImageNet with ResNet-18 teachers, vary poisoning rate (1-5%), target class (0, 40, 80), distillation weight (0.5-0.7), trigger strength (patch area, frequency amplitude), size of the search pool, the rule's distance metric (L1 instead of L2) and grayscale evaluation. Result: teacher success at 1% poisoning is 70.23% (spatial) and 99.68% (frequency), rising to 99.24% and 100% at 3%; student success is 79-86% (spatial) and 97.1-97.6% (frequency) across the three target classes; at distillation weight 0.5 the frequency variant keeps 94.82% while the spatial variant falls to 52.51%; very weak triggers or tiny search pools reduce success; L1 distance (99.97% / 95.08%) and grayscale inputs (99.77% / 99.96%) keep it high.

Vary what the student is distilled on while keeping the poisoned teacher fixed. Setup: distil on COCO images, on synthetic OpenGL renderings, and on a 50-class ImageNet subset with and without the target class. Result: COCO gives 100% attack success for both variants and OpenGL 94.76% / 100%, despite low student clean accuracy (about 32% and 15%) from weak proxy data; the 50-class subset gives 94.68% / 99.96% when it includes the target class and 0.00% for both when it does not.

Check whether the backdoor lives in channels clean images also use. Setup: define the 4 or 8 channels contributing most to the target logit on triggered inputs as backdoor channels, and measure their activation-weighted contribution percentile on 20,000 random clean ImageNet images relative to all channels, in teachers (T) and students (S). Result: trigger-backdoor channels sit at low clean-image percentiles (top-4: BadNets 19.6, Blend 21.2, Refool 9.9, WaNet 0.6), while relabelling-backdoor channels sit much higher (frequency teacher 28.3 and student 70.6; spatial teacher 79.4 and student 45.2), within the range of ordinary clean channels. Under the 19 ImageNet-C corruptions the share of rule-positive images stays near the poisoning rates (weighted 6.70% and 5.58%).

Rule out that the backdoor is just a universal adversarial perturbation in disguise. Setup: on the ResNet-50 protocol, compare a universal adversarial perturbation for the same target class against both relabelling variants under Gaussian blur (kernel 3-9) and JPEG compression (quality 70-10) applied before inference. Result: the universal perturbation falls from 82.90% to 12.75-25.94% under blur and 0.18-34.90% under JPEG, while the relabelling variants stay at 99.35-100% under every setting.

Run standard backdoor defences. Setup: mitigation by fine-tuning, fine-pruning, SAU, CLP (pruning threshold swept, best point under a clean-accuracy constraint) and OTBR, given 1% of ImageNet where data are needed; detection by STRIP and Spectral at a 5% false-positive rate, reporting effective attack success after rejected inputs are removed. Result: the frequency variant on ResNet-50 keeps 99.8-100% after all five mitigations and Spectral, and 38.4% after STRIP; the spatial variant on ResNet-50 is removed by CLP (0.0%) and weakened by fine-tuning (35.2%) and fine-pruning (43.6%). On ResNet-18 the frequency variant is removed by fine-tuning (3.0%) but survives the rest (65.7-97.3%). Trigger backdoors are removed by some defences and not others (e.g. WaNet by fine-tuning, fine-pruning and SAU; Blend by none of the mitigations).

notes: The paper's Table 5 is captioned 'ASR down-arrow' but reports attacker-side success; treated as higher-is-stronger.
